# Investment Memorandum

## 1. Executive Summary

- On January 31, 2024, Core Alaska, LLC and its guarantors executed Waiver No. 2 and Amendment No. 4 to their Credit and Guarantee Agreement with ING Capital LLC and Macquarie Bank Limited.
- Core Alaska, LLC, a Delaware limited liability company, serves as the Borrower, with guarantors including Contango Ore, Inc., Alaska Gold Torrent, LLC, and Contango Minerals Alaska, LLC - all entities within the Contango mining group.
- The transaction addresses technical Events of Default that occurred when Contango created a new subsidiary, Contango Mining Canada Inc. (CMC), in July 2023 and established BMO bank accounts without timely compliance with credit agreement requirements for subsidiary guarantor status and account disclosure.
- The original Credit and Guarantee Agreement was dated May 17, 2023, with ING Capital LLC as Administrative Agent and Macquarie Bank Limited as Collateral Agent, with ING Capital LLC and Macquarie Bank Limited serving as Mandated Lead Arrangers.
- The purpose is to waive the technical defaults and formally incorporate the new Canadian subsidiary and its bank accounts into the credit structure while implementing restrictive covenants on account balances.

## 2. Investment Highlights & Risks

### Key Strengths / Credit Positives:
• Established lender relationships with reputable institutions (ING Capital LLC and Macquarie Bank Limited) providing continuity in the credit facility
• Proactive resolution of technical defaults demonstrates borrower's commitment to compliance and transparency with lenders
• All collateral documents and security interests remain in full force and effect, preserving lender protections
• The defaults were technical/administrative in nature rather than financial performance-related issues

### Principal Risks and Mitigating Factors:
• Recent history of compliance failures, though technical in nature, indicates potential gaps in credit administration processes
• Expansion into Canadian operations through new subsidiary may introduce additional operational and regulatory complexities
• Strict limitations imposed on BMO account balances (aggregate maximum of $200,000) suggest lender caution regarding foreign account management
• Multiple covenant deadlines (10-30 days) create near-term execution risk if not met timely
